equity_bridge.note: Agreed sale to Asahi for ~$2.3bn (announced 17-Dec-25; Kenyan court cleared Apr-26; completion expected by 31-Dec-26). Less ~$250m estimated Kenyan CGT, transaction costs and the $85m recycled translation loss is non-cash. EABL revenue/EBITDA removed from FY0 base.

equity_bridge.item: Royal Challengers Bengaluru sale, attributable net proceeds
equity_bridge.note: USL sale of RCB for ~$1.78bn (Mar-26), held for sale at 30-Jun-26, completion expected FY27. Less ~14% Indian capital-gains tax, x 57.21% Diageo ownership of USL (NCI share excluded because NCI is charged in the flows).

equity_bridge.item: Fair value of debt hedges (FX and interest-rate derivatives)
equity_bridge.note: Company net borrowings reconciliation, 30-Jun-26: -$194m (asset) offsets the USD value of hedged non-USD bonds inside total_debt.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: management FY27-29 guide (low-single-digit organic net sales CAGR) cross-checked to the 5yr USD revenue CAGR of 2.8%
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (2.7-3.1%) diverges >30% from EPS CAGR (-12.6% / -26.5%): EPS is crushed by FY25-26 exceptional impairments and restructuring ($1.4bn and $2.5bn) and equity growth is suppressed by FY18-24 buybacks (~$10bn). Neither is a usable growth anchor; revenue and management guidance used instead.
historical_growth.notes: All CAGRs in USD. FY2026 vs FY2023 uses the USD-restated FY2023 comparatives from the FY2024 20-F (net sales $20,555m, OCF $3,636m, capex $1,417m, SBC $58m, EPS 196.3c). The FY2021 start point is GBP converted at the FY21 average GBP/USD ~1.344 (flows) and Jun-21 ~1.38 (equity) - approximate. Owner FCF = reported FCF (OCF - capex) - SBC; interest income not stripped (net debt). The 3yr FCF CAGR (+13.4%) starts from the FY23 trough (maturing-stock and inventory build) and the 5yr (-4.7%) from the FY21 post-COVID peak; neither is a forward rate. SBC-adjusted and reported FCF CAGRs are essentially identical: SBC is immaterial at 0.2-0.4% of sales. EPS is per ordinary share (x4 for per-ADS).

scenario_narratives.base: Diageo follows the path its new CEO laid out at the FY26 results: FY27 is a reset year with broadly flat organic sales as North America (about 40% of sales) shrinks mid-single-digit in a US spirits market down ~3%, then low-single-digit growth FY28-29 with North America recovering only gradually while Europe (Guinness), India (USL premiumization), LatAm and Asia grow 3-5%. The ~$1bn Accelerate/operating-framework savings mostly fund reinvestment in A&P, so the adjusted EBITDA margin creeps up ~1.5pp to ~36% rather than leaping, and ~$850m of restructuring cash plus a permanent ~0.6pp exceptional drag are charged in the flows. Disposals (EABL ~$2.3bn, RCB ~$1.78bn) take leverage back into the 2.5-3x range by FY27 without new equity. Owner FCF recovers from a guided ~$2bn trough in FY27 to ~$3.5-4bn by FY30.
scenario_narratives.bull: The US destocking cycle ends in FY27, Dave Lewis's North America reset (share recovery, Mexico/Canada supply-chain reshoring blunting the tariff hit) returns the region to growth from FY28, Guinness's doubled Kildare capacity sustains double-digit beer growth and Indian premiumization compounds; group sales grow ~5% FY29-31 and more of the $1bn savings drops through, taking the EBITDA margin to ~37.5%, near Diageo's FY19-22 peak economics. Deleveraging to ~2x by FY29 reopens buybacks.
scenario_narratives.bear: The North America malaise is structural rather than cyclical: moderation, GLP-1 adoption and younger consumers drinking less keep the US spirits category shrinking, tequila and vodka keep losing share, and US tariffs on Mexico- and Canada-made spirits (~40-45% of US sales; ~$200m OP exposure) stick. Group sales fall in FY27 and grow only ~2% thereafter; the savings programme is consumed by price investment and tariffs, so the margin stalls around 33% and more impairments of past acquisitions (Turkiye, Don Papa, Aviation precedents) follow. Leverage stays near 3x, constraining the dividend.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Normalized, mid-cycle owner-FCF DCF in USD per ADS. The base is pro forma FY26 adjusted EBITDA (ex exceptionals, ex EABL), with restructuring cash charged explicitly and a permanent exceptional drag, so neither the depressed FY26 reported earnings nor the FY22-24 post-COVID peak is extrapolated. The disposals and the Moet Hennessy stake sit in the bridge; leverage is charged once, through the relevered beta and debt cost.
key_risks_to_valuation: North America (about 40% of sales) recovery slower than the guided multi-year path; structural moderation/GLP-1 demand loss
US tariffs on Mexico/Canada-sourced tequila and Canadian whisky (~40-45% of US sales)
EABL net proceeds estimated (~$2.05bn): EABL stand-alone revenue/EBITDA not disclosed in the 20-F; ~$1,050m/$250m removal is an estimate
Moet Hennessy stake valued at ~$4.0bn vs $5.3bn book on trough cognac/champagne earnings
Further brand/market impairments (Turkiye, Don Papa, Aviation precedents) signalling M&A value destruction not captured in capex
Terminal value cap-bound at 17x owner FCF: value is sensitive to the exit multiple more than to terminal growth

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (regular close); 52-week range 72.45-102.74
data_sources.financials: Diageo Form 20-F FY2026 (income statement, cash flow statement, notes 8, 14, 17, 18; non-GAAP reconciliations pp. 209-211: free cash flow, adjusted EBITDA $6,650m, net borrowings $20,482m, tax rate before exceptional items 24.3%); Form 20-F FY2024 for USD-restated FY2022-23 comparatives; DEO_Metrics.csv / DEO.duckdb core_metrics and kpis
data_sources.qualitative: DEO_Analysis.json (2026-10-04): FY27 guidance (broadly flat organic net sales, LMSD organic OP growth, FCF c.$2bn after exceptionals), FY27-29 guidance (LSD organic sales CAGR, MSD organic OP CAGR, cumulative FCF c.$8bn after c.$850m exceptional cash), leverage target 2.5-3x FY27 and ~2x FY29

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2026 reported net sales $19,643m less an estimated ~$1,050m for EABL + Kenyan spirits (held for sale 30-Jun-26, sale to Asahi expected to close by 31-Dec-26). EABL's stand-alone net sales are not disclosed in the 20-F; estimate from the Africa region ($1,642m net sales, $356m pre-exceptional OP) of which East Africa is the majority. Pro forma removes ~$250m of adjusted EBITDA (EABL EBITDA net of the Guinness licence royalty Diageo retains). Disposal proceeds enter the equity bridge instead.
inputs.share_count_basis: ADS-equivalents: FY2026 diluted weighted ordinary shares 2,231m (20-F income statement: 2,224m basic + 7m dilutive) divided by 4, because 1 DEO ADS = 4 ordinary shares (20-F FY2026 lines 8045/12964). NOTE: the brief stated 1 ADS = 1 share; the filing says four. All per-share values in this file are per ADS so they compare to the NYSE price. CSV EPS (0.781) is per ORDINARY share - multiply by 4 for per-ADS. Held FLAT: SBC (0.2% of sales) is expensed in the flows and no non-SBC issuance is expected.
inputs.net_debt_note: core_metrics FY2026 total_debt $21,511m (borrowings due within one year 2,449 + after one year 19,062, EXCLUDING lease liabilities) less cash $1,520m. Company 'net borrowings' $20,482m additionally includes lease liabilities $685m (excluded here under lease treatment B) and derivative hedges -$194m (added back in equity_bridge).
inputs.interest_income_note: Not stripped: the company is in net debt (~$20bn), so the net-cash double-count rule does not apply. Finance income $384m sits below EBITDA and is not in the unlevered flows.
inputs.sbc_source: 20-F FY2026 cash flow note 'Share-based incentive plans' $44m (FY25 $59m, FY24 $43m). EquityAwardTaxes = 0 (UK plans settled from employee benefit trusts; 'net sale of own shares for share schemes' is a small inflow). Combined figure not separately published.
inputs.buyback_note: No buybacks in FY25-FY26 ($987m in FY24); programme suspended while deleveraging. Flat count is a modelling convention here, not funded by repurchases - immaterial because SBC is 0.2% of sales.
inputs.fx_note: Flows in USD (Diageo's reporting currency since FY2024); NYSE ADS quoted in USD; no conversion. Historical CAGRs: FY2022-23 use the USD-restated comparatives from the FY2024 20-F (net sales $20,516m / $20,555m; OCF $5,213m / $3,636m; capex $1,457m / $1,417m; basic EPS 184.6c / 196.3c). FY2016-21 GBP rows were converted at approximate fiscal-year average GBP/USD (FY21 1.344) for flows and year-end rates (Jun-21 1.38, Jun-23 1.27) for equity - approximate, used for trend only, never in the cash-flow base.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-02T20:00:02Z regular close (Friday NYSE close; valuation dated Sunday 2026-10-04)
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD build. Risk-free ~4.2% (10y UST); ERP 5.0%; beta 0.95 = unlevered ~0.65 relevered at D/E ~0.46 (market cap ~$47bn vs ~$22bn debt incl. leases) -> cost of equity ~9.0%. Marginal pre-tax cost of debt ~5.3% (BBB+/A- USD 10y at ~UST+110bp; FY26 cash interest $1,044m / ~$21.5bn = 4.9% running) -> ~4.0% after 25% tax. Weights E 68% / D 32% -> 7.4%, rounded to 7.5%. The above-target leverage (3.1x) is charged through the relevered beta and the marginal debt cost, NOT as an ad-hoc premium; scenario risk lives in the flows (same WACC in all three scenarios).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost: lease_cost_pct_path 0.85% of net sales = FY26 lease principal $126m + ~$35m lease interest; lease liabilities ($685m) EXCLUDED from net debt; da_pct_path is D&A ex right-of-use depreciation (FY26 pre-exceptional D&A $749m less ROU depreciation $151m less ~$40m EABL = ~3.0% of pro forma sales), so the lease is charged once.
inputs.nci_treatment: Attributable-only flows: NCI leakage folded into cash_tax_rate_path. Pre-exceptional NCI profit $227m FY26 (USL 42.79% NCI, Shuijingfang 36.35%, Ketel One 50%, EABL 35%); ex-EABL ~$180m = ~4% of NOPAT, adding ~3pp to the 24.3% pre-exceptional tax rate -> ~27.5% combined leakage. No NCI deduction in the bridge (charge once). Calibration: FY26 EBIT ~$5.9bn x (1-27.5%) less after-tax net finance ~$0.62bn plus associates $0.22bn = ~$3.9bn vs reported pre-exceptional attributable profit ~$3.7bn - within non-operating noise (pension finance, hyperinflation).
inputs.exceptional_items_treatment: FY2026 exceptional operating items $2,527m (Turkiye/Mey Icki impairment $786m, Don Papa $287m, restructuring ~$908m, accelerated depreciation) and FY25 $1,369m are excluded from the base via adjusted EBITDA ($6,650m FY26, $6,645m FY25). They are NOT ignored: ebitda_margin_path carries an explicit cash drag of 2.6pp FY27, 1.8pp FY28, 1.0pp FY29 (~$1.04bn: the guided c.$850m FY27-29 exceptional cash cost, front-loaded, plus ~$190m overrun allowance) and 0.6pp (~$115-130m/yr) in perpetuity, the typical run-rate of recurring restructuring/other exceptional cash in normal years (FY24 net credit $56m; FY25 cash restructuring/non-operating spend $45m; FY26 $184m; recurring brand write-downs are the non-cash echo of past M&A and are not re-charged).
inputs.associates_treatment: Adjusted EBITDA excludes the share of associates ($218m FY26, mostly the 34% Moet Hennessy stake) and the unlevered flows exclude the $116m dividends received; the stake therefore enters the equity bridge at value (matching-asset rule).
inputs.normalization: Mid-cycle / normalized: base starts from pro forma FY26 adjusted EBITDA (34.7% of pro forma sales pre-SBC), NOT from FY26 reported operating profit ($3,156m, depressed by exceptionals) and NOT from the FY22-24 peak (organic +6-8% post-COVID restock years). Calibration to guidance: management guides FY27 FCF c.$2bn after exceptionals and cumulative FY27-29 FCF c.$8bn after c.$850m exceptional cash; the base case's unlevered owner FCF FY27-29, converted to the company's levered consolidated definition (+NCI share, -after-tax net interest ~$0.55-0.6bn/yr, +associate dividends), lands ~$8.9bn, ~$0.9bn (~11%) above the c.$8bn guide; the residual is unexplained by disclosed components (likely disposal-related tax, Moet Hennessy termination fees and working-capital phasing in the guide) and is worth ~$1.5/ADS in PV. FY27 alone models ~$2.8bn levered vs the c.$2bn guide - the guide's FY27 is a trough the model does not fully replicate. The bear case's FY27-29 cumulative (~$8.2bn) sits on the guide.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, three scenarios, 10-year horizon, per dcf-methods SKILL.md routing row 'Operating company, non-US or cyclical' (owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md). Diageo is an operating branded-spirits/beer company: not a bank, REIT, LIC or holdco. No prior DCF and no MEMORY.md entry: fresh build. Currency: USD flows (Diageo switched reporting currency from GBP in FY2024; the GBP->USD step in the CSV between FY2023 and FY2024 is that redenomination, not a units bug), USD quote. Per-ADS basis (1 ADS = 4 ordinary shares). FY0 is pro forma ex-EABL (see base_revenue_note); RCB proceeds and EABL proceeds in the equity bridge. SBC is immaterial (0.2% of sales) so the house/street band is narrow but non-degenerate. Price is a regular-session close.

bear.narrative: North America decline proves structural (moderation, GLP-1, Gen-Z drinking less); tariffs on Mexico/Canada-made tequila and Crown Royal stick; savings are competed away; margin stalls ~33%.

base.growth_rates_rationale: FY27 +0.5% = guided 'broadly flat' organic (North America down mid-single-digit, US market -3%) plus modest price/FX. FY28-29 3.0-3.5% = guided low-single-digit FY27-29 CAGR, with North America (~40% of sales) only gradually returning to LSD while the rest grows 3-5% (Guinness capacity, India via USL, LatAm). FY30-31 4% as North America normalises; fades to 3% (USD nominal) by FY35.
base.ebitda_margin_path_rationale: Adjusted EBITDA pre-SBC, IFRS-16 basis, NET of exceptional cash drag. Underlying margin 34.7% FY26 pro forma -> ~35.3% FY27 (low-to-mid-single-digit organic OP growth on flat sales, ~40% of $850m operating-framework savings), ~36.0% FY29 (guided mid-single-digit OP CAGR on LSD sales), plateau ~36.4%; most of the ~$1bn savings is reinvested in A&P per management. Less exceptional cash drag 2.6/1.8/1.0pp FY27-29 (front-loaded: ~$490m/$350m/$200m, i.e. the guided c.$850m plus ~$190m overrun) and 0.6pp thereafter.
base.capex_pct_path_rationale: FY24-26 capex 7.4%/8.0%/6.1% of net sales; FY27-28 held ~7% for Guinness 'Brewery 2' (~EUR400m), supply agility and S/4HANA follow-on; glides to 5.5% (pre-2022 norm ~4.5-5.5%) by FY32.
base.cash_tax_rate_path_rationale: Pre-exceptional tax rate 24.3% FY26 plus ~3pp NCI leakage (see inputs.nci_treatment); +0.5pp FY27-29 for catch-up after FY26's low $817m cash tax (restructuring deductions).
base.wc_capture_pct_rationale: Negative: inventory (incl. maturing whisky/tequila stock) is ~38% of net sales against payables ~30%; growth consumes ~40c of working capital per $1 of incremental sales.
base.terminal_cap_multiple_rationale: 17x terminal owner FCF (~10-11x EV/EBITDA), below the 20.5x Gordon value at 7.5%/2.5%: a mature staples brand portfolio, with today's ~10x EV/adj-EBITDA as the reference. Cap binds.
base.narrative: Reset then recovery on management's own path.

bull.narrative: US destocking ends in FY27 and North America returns to LSD-MSD growth from FY28; Guinness capacity, India premiumization and RTDs carry the rest to 5%+; more of the $1bn savings drops through.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 17x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: the thesis rests on an unproven turnaround under a CEO in his first year, management's own guide is for a multi-year North America recovery, tariffs are a live regulatory risk outside Diageo's control, and leverage (3.1x) limits room for error. Base 50%: the guide is specific and the cost programme is ~85% delivered on its first tranche. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it needs several independent things to go right at once (US category recovery, tariff relief, savings dropping through).

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
